newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-WILMOTS BRILLIANCE KEEPS SCHALKE DREAM ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WILMOTS BRILLIANCE KEEPS SCHALKE DREAM ALIVE.

text.p: A spectacular goal from Belgian Marc Wilmots kept alive Schalke's dream of making European soccer history when they beat Internazionale Milan 1-0 at home in the first leg of the UEFA Cup final on Wednesday.

Just as a dismal game seemed to be heading towards a goalless draw, Wilmots picked up the ball in the middle of the Inter half in the 70th minute, took a few strides towards the edge of the box and fired the ball low into the left-hand corner.

Apart from the piece of brilliance, Schalke, who have never won a European trophy and last won a domestic title back in 1972, did not produce any other clear goalscoring chances in a match which rarely got above the standard of a mediocre domestic league encounter.
But the goal gives the Germans some hope to take to Milan for the second leg in two weeks when Inter will be looking to win the trophy for the third time after 1991 and 1994.

Inter, who were missing French defender Jocelyn Angloma, English midfielder Paul Ince and Frenchman Youri Djorkaeff because of suspension, also struggled to get their game together and did not have a dangerous shot on goal.
But the Italians are sure to take the game to the Germans in the second leg in front of their home fans.
